text: Illustration of Analysis Process • Infrastructure example – Q: “Are [observed events] a terrorism risk?” – A: Rapid reconstitution, low consequences, high mitigation cost  probably not a risk worthy of further mitigation • Transportation example – Q: “Which terrorism scenarios should ___ worry about?” – A: That depends… • Easy scenario: onboard shooter – many comparable targets  likely to happen somewhere, not specific to ____ • Harder scenario requiring more resources: few comparable targets, resources available to terrorists  scenario should be of concern • Much harder scenario requiring more resources & special training: harder to do and lower consequences  scenario is unlikely INMM(TRAM) 7/15/09 11 Summary & Conclusions • The Total Risk Assessment Method helps analysts iteratively identify, refine and rank scenarios – Ranked for each target by adversary attractiveness • Highest consequence for particular adversary resources – Relative scenario likelihoods tied to objective criteria • Scenario cohort groups: targets and scenarios with similar characteristics provide global risk context • We are NOT “calculating” probability of attack! • Risk management: helping decision makers understand which scenarios to mitigate – Must reexamine screened scenarios to understand degree of improvement and remaining risks Scenarios and vulnerabilities, without their global context, are an insufficient basis for making risk mitigation and risk management decisions.
